title: Knowledge check: Calling External APIs from Express

questions.prompt: In Calling External APIs from Express, which statement best describes HTTP clients available in Node.js?
options: Connect this syllabus point to Calling External APIs from Express: state the expected behavior, identify a realistic edge case, and choose a test or observation that proves the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.
Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.
Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.
Keep the interface predictable for its client: use clear resource boundaries, explicit request/response formats, correct status codes, validation and tests for failure cases.
questions.answer_key: Keep the interface predictable for its client: use clear resource boundaries, explicit request/response formats, correct status codes, validation and tests for failure cases.
questions.explanation: Keep the interface predictable for its client: use clear resource boundaries, explicit request/response formats, correct status codes, validation and tests for failure cases.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying Calling External APIs from Express?
options: Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.

Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
questions.answer_key: Uploads, API calls, and webhooks cross trust boundaries. Limit file sizes, verify content and signatures, use timeouts, retry only safe operations, and make duplicate webhook delivery idempotent.
questions.explanation: Uploads, API calls, and webhooks cross trust boundaries. Limit file sizes, verify content and signatures, use timeouts, retry only safe operations, and make duplicate webhook delivery idempotent.
